shelled snails text index | photo index Phylum Mollusca

Class Gastropoda > Family Strombidae Vitate conch snail
Doxander vittatus apicatus
Family Strombidaeupdated Jul 2023

Where seen? This conch snail was seen alive at St John’s Island among seagrases. And Beting Bronok among seagrasses growing on soft silty ground..

Features: 6-8cm, elsewhere up to 10cm. Shell thick, heavy, long and narrow, lip flared slightly wavy. The flared shell protects the long proboscis as the animal sweeps the bottom for titbits. Large eyes on eyestalks, each eyestalk has a tentacle, the purpose of which is not known. Like other conch snails, it hops using the knife-like operculum at the tip of a long muscular foot. St John’s Island, Jul 16*
*St John’s Island, Jul 16* *Beting Bronok, Jul 2023
